_comment: Sensitivity and version metadata for the Meridian corpus. Kept OUT of the
documents themselves on purpose: front-matter would be embedded along with
the body and pollute the vectors, so a label meant for the pipeline would
quietly become part of the meaning being searched.
Retrieval must filter on 'sensitivity' BEFORE ranking. A restricted chunk that
reaches the ranker has already failed, even if the generated prose looks clean.
lab_3.py globs corpus/*.md non-recursively, so corpus/restricted/ is invisible
to it and Lab 3's chunk counts and narrative are unchanged.
_canary_comment: Exact strings that must never appear in an answer served to a general employee.
These are matched literally, not classified — a known synthetic value either is
or is not present in the output. That is structural string matching, not 'is this
PII', which stays an LLM-judge question. The two layers answer different things:
canaries catch verbatim leakage with zero false positives; the judge catches
